title: Unified Inference: Product PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (v12)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, design specifications, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the Unified Inference product line (v12). The goal is to provide a single reference for engineering, product, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams during the v12 launch and subsequent quarters.

1) Product overview

Objective:
- Deliver a single, consistent inference API across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments with predictable latency, cost controls, and first-class observability.

Key capabilities (v12 focus):
- Unified API surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Cost-aware routing & automatic fallback to model variants.
- Advanced Redwood Optimize integrations: model/quantization recommendations surfaced in Console.
- Improved rollout controls: canary, A/B, auto-fallback, and region-aware policies.

Primary personas:
- Product engineers building LLM features (PLG motion)
- Platform/infra teams consuming Dedicated/Private
- Security/compliance owners evaluating Private deployments

Success metrics (KPIs):
- API latency p50/p95 reductions against v11: p95 <= 250ms for small text-gen (<= 512 tokens) on Hosted.
- Cost per 1k tokens improvement: >= 12% reduction via batching/quantization defaults.
- Adoption: 20 enterprise Dedicated deals signed in Q1 post-launch.
- Quality: <1.5% regression rate on top-20 prompt sets over 90 days (monitored via Eval pipeline).

2) PRD: Requirements and acceptance criteria

A. Functional requirements:
- FR-01: Unified endpoints /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings with identical request/response semantics across deployments. (AC: schema validation tests pass; SDKs return same typed objects)
- FR-02: Model routing policy engine allowing rules by latency SLO, cost budget, and region. (AC: routing rules can be created in Console and enforced in runtime simulator)
- FR-03: Redwood Optimize recommendations surfaced in Console and REST API (batching, quantization profiles). (AC: sample 10-workload recommendation set delivered)
- FR-04: Rollout controls: percentage-based canary, route-based A/B, and automatic fallback to safe models on errors. (AC: rollout APIs + audit logs exist and demo available)

B. Non-functional requirements:
- NFR-01: SLO compliance: 99.9% availability per-hosted-region; p95 latency targets defined per model class. (AC: synthetic tests run daily; failure budget tracking)
- NFR-02: Observability: traceable requestID across gateway->runtime->cache with token-level cost attribution. (AC: logs + Console charts available for sample customer)
- NFR-03: Security: support for KMS/HSM key wrapping in Private and Dedicated. (AC: KMS integration tests and secure-config doc)
- NFR-04: Scale: support for burst to 2x baseline throughput for Dedicated pools. (AC: load tests pass per capacity plan)

C. Acceptance test checklist:
- End-to-end SDK test matrix across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (languages: Python, Go, Node).
- Regression evals run on canonical prompt sets; threshold: no more than 1.5% quality regression on top-20 prompts.
- Cost/regression smoke: end-to-end measurement for batching & quant suggestions showing expected token-cost delta.

Requirements table (overview):
| ID | Type | Priority | Owner | Acceptance Criteria |
| FR-01 | Functional | P0 | API/Product | Schema parity across deployments |
| FR-02 | Functional | P0 | Runtime | Routing rules + simulator |
| FR-03 | Functional | P1 | Optimize | Recommendation API + Console UI |
| NFR-01 | Non-functional | P0 | SRE | SLOs defined + daily synthetic tests |

3) Design specification (high level)

Architecture components:
- Control Plane (Console + Policy Engine): routes, rollout configs, recommendations.
- Public API Gateway: authentication, per-tenant quotas, routing decisions, request canonicalization.
- Serving Runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine, kernel selection, KV cache.
- Cache Layer: prefix/KV cache with per-tenant eviction and TTL policies.
- Telemetry & Observability: request traces, token-level costing, model evaluation telemetry.

Sequence (happy path):
1. Client calls /v1/generate with model: "rwd-unified-1" and prompt/policy hints.
2. Gateway authenticates and looks up tenant config, quotas, and routing policy.
3. Policy Engine decides target model variant and serving cluster.
4. Gateway forwards request to runtime; runtime checks prefix cache and resumes KV if warm.
5. Runtime streams tokens back through gateway; token-level cost is emitted to telemetry pipeline.

API contract (example request/response):
- Request (JSON):
{
  "model": "rwd-unified-1",
  "input": "Translate to French: \"Hello\"",
  "max_tokens": 64,
  "response_format": "text"
}
- Response (JSON stream/event):
{
  "request_id": "req_123",
  "token": "Bonjour",
  "token_index": 1,
  "partial_cost_microtokens": 42
}

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Kernel selection on-the-fly (per-sequence-length profiling) favors latency SLOs over maximizing GPU throughput for low-latency tiers. Trade-off: slightly higher cost for ultra-low latency.
- Automatic fallback prefers model family with same tokenizer to avoid output regression. Trade-off: may pick a larger model variant in rare cases increasing cost.

Operational considerations:
- Canary windows default to 5% traffic for 24 hours with automatic rollback on error-rate delta > 0.5% or p95 increase > 20%.
- Cost guardrails: routing engine enforces per-route cost budgets; beyond budget, route is throttled or routed to cheaper variant.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 4 quarters)

Q1 2027 (Launch quarter) - Stabilize & Grow:
- Finalize v12 SDKs and Console UX for recommendations.
- Expand model catalog with 3 verified quantized variants.
- Sales enablement: enterprise kit + Dedicated ROI calculator.

Q2 2027 - Performance & Economics:
- Continuous batching improvements and adaptive batching policies.
- Advanced quantization profiles (mixed-precision heuristics) exposed in Optimize.

Q3 2027 - Private/Compliance:
- Harden Private deployment automation for air-gapped environments.
- SOC2/ISO evidence bundles for inference telemetry.

Q4 2027 - Platform Integrations:
- Marketplace integrations and partner-managed Dedicated regions.
- New A/B experimentation APIs with integrated quality monitoring.

Cross-cutting themes:
- Developer-first: reduce friction for first-call latency and quickstarts.
- Cost transparency: token-level unit economics surfaced to customers.
- Reliability: automatic fallbacks and improved SLO observability.

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Tiers (high level):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation pricing + per-embedding unit. Discounts for committed spend.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commits with baseline throughput and burst. Unit economics improved by ~30% vs Hosted per committed GPU.
- Private (enterprise): platform license + professional services for on-prem or VPC with KMS integrations.

Pricing components to note:
- Token-unit pricing by model-class (e.g., small/medium/large).
- Capacity pricing for Dedicated by GPU type and guaranteed vCPU/RAM for orchestration nodes.
- Add-ons: Enhanced observability retention, compliance package, premium SLA.

Packaging guidance for GTM:
- Offer a Dedicated starter pack (3-month trial at a discounted commit) for platform teams.
- Include a migration guide and cost-savings calculator that converts a customers current token spend into expected Dedicated ROI.

6) Release notes (v12)

Release version: v12 (2026-12-15)
Highlights:
- Unified API parity across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Model routing policy engine (beta) with Console UI.
- Redwood Optimize: first-run recommendations visible in Console and exported via API.
- Improved rollout controls (percent canary, automated rollback rules).

Migration notes for customers:
- SDKs: clients pinned to v12 SDKs will get identical request/response objects; older SDKs may need minor field renames (see migration appendix).
- Rollouts: customers using custom routing must review policy mappings; default heuristics will attempt to map older rules but require validation.

Known issues and workarounds:
- KMS rotation in early Private installs requires a manual service restart; documented in onprem-packaging/runbook.
- Very large embeddings (>16k tokens) may experience degraded throughput on certain Dedicated device families; recommend batching smaller requests.

7) Launch & rollout checklist (numbered)

1. Final E2E tests green across languages and deployment modes.
2. QA sign-off on regression eval results.
3. Console UI accessibility review completed.
4. Documentation published: quickstarts, SDK changelogs, migration guide.
5. Sales enablement: pricing decks, ROI calculator, customer-facing launch kit.
6. Oncall runbook & SRE playbook published with post-deploy monitoring thresholds.
7. Gradual ramp plan: 0->5% traffic (24h) -> 25% (72h) -> 100% (7 days) with automated rollback triggers.
